newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta agency calls for barley vote extension.
newsitem.headline: Alberta agency calls for barley vote extension.

text.p: The Alberta Grain Commission said on Friday it was calling for an extension to a key government of Canada plebiscite on barley marketing after receiving complaints from farmers.

The commission said numerous Alberta barley growers, who were being asked if they wanted to sell their production on the open market or maintain the Canadian Wheat Board's monopoly on export sales, complained they did not receive ballots before today's deadline for mailing.

"Unrealistic time lines were set in terms of the deadline for affidavit requests and mailing ballots. No reasonable effort was made to accommodate this error, even when we asked," Alberta Grain Commission chairman Ken Moholitny said in a statement.
"For this reason, were are asking the federal government to extend the deadline for voting so that barley farmers are not denied the opportunity to register their opinion,' he said.
The commission said it believed there were flaws in the registration of voters.
As of last Wednesday, 50,000 ballots were mailed back, consulting firm KPMG said. Approximately 76,000 barley growers are eligible to vote.
About 70 percent of Alberta's barley is used in the local feed market. The rest is marketed through the Canadian Wheat Board.
